README: Round-2 SmartGrade prototype dataset. Designed to be imported into Supabase/PostgreSQL or used as JSON/CSV seed data.
Technical values are taken from the supplied Jindal Stainless PDFs. Where a source does not provide a field, the dataset leaves it blank/NA instead of inventing a value.
Qualitative tags such as corrosion_level, formability_level and weldability_level are normalized from source wording for prototype logic. Keep the source_text field alongside them.
Lower/Moderate/Higher are prototype relative bands, not Jindal quotations. They are intentionally editable and must not be presented as live pricing.

Only exact grade/site PCF assessment records from the supplied finalized sustainability dataset are marked as assessed. 409L is NOT treated as 409; missing exact product-level evidence remains unavailable.

Use hard constraints first; then rank surviving candidates using configurable weights for engineering fit, corrosion, temperature, fabrication, cost and evidence. Missing data must not become an automatic failure or zero score.

The Expert_Validation sheet contains demo records showing a complex recommendation submitted for review, reviewer decision/note, and report status. These are sample workflow data, not real human approvals.
The Before_You_Buy sheet provides a demo checklist record covering specification, certification, MTC, dimensions, finish and quantity.
For implementation, seed grades/properties/applications/cost/sustainability/sources first. Then use Recommendation_Scenarios as demo/test cases and Expert_Validation as the validation workflow seed.

Recommendation_Scenarios: I need a welded component for an outdoor coastal structure. It should have high strength. Cost matters but performance is important.

2205 combines 450 MPa minimum yield strength with better corrosion resistance than 316L in various environments; 316L is a lower-strength corrosion-resistant alternative. 2101 demonstrates a lower-Ni duplex alternative with high strength.
Exact product form, design code, temperature, welding procedure, and current procurement specification.
I need a stainless steel tank for food processing. It will be welded and cleaned frequently. Cost should be moderate.

304L is a low-carbon welded-condition option with broad food/process applications; J204Cu is documented as a cost/property bridge with food-processing applications; 316L adds Mo-based corrosion performance for more demanding conditions.
Exact cleaning chemicals, chloride concentration, temperature, finish and food-contact specification.
Exhaust component, 750-800°C, welded, cost-sensitive, moderate corrosion exposure.

409L is explicitly designed for automotive exhaust systems and oxidation resistance to approximately 800°C; 321 is documented for high-temperature exhaust stacks/manifolds and 450-900°C service context.
Exact exhaust chemistry, component temperature history, thickness, weld procedure and durability requirement.
Chemical production component operating around 600°C; welded; corrosion resistance and elevated-temperature stability are important.
321 is explicitly a Ti-stabilized 304 grade for 450-900°C applications and improved intergranular corrosion resistance in that range.
Pressure code, exact thermal cycle, process chemistry and product form.
I need deep-drawn kitchenware. Good formability is important and I want to keep the material cost down.

J204Cu is explicitly positioned as a cost/property bridge with high formability and cookware applications; J4 is documented for deep-drawn kitchen equipment and cookware; 304 is the benchmark general-purpose option.
Food-contact requirements, exact forming operation and product form.
Offshore process piping for chloride-containing media. High strength and corrosion resistance are both critical; welded fabrication required.
Offshore / chloride piping and process equipment
2205 is documented for chloride-containing media, offshore structures and high yield strength. 2101 offers high strength and corrosion resistance comparable to 316L with lower Ni/Mo content.
Design pressure, exact chloride chemistry, temperature, weld procedure, corrosion allowance and code requirements.
I need a stainless steel material for an indoor appliance/decorative panel. Corrosion resistance is needed but cost is important.

430 is explicitly used for decorative panels and appliances and is positioned for mildly corrosive environments; 304 offers broader corrosion/formability performance; J4 provides a cost/formability alternative in documented applications.
Surface finish, forming operation and exact corrosion environment.
Seawater handling equipment with high chloride exposure. Corrosion resistance is critical; welded fabrication required.

904L is explicitly documented for desalination and seawater handling and has high chloride pitting resistance; 316L and 2205 provide comparison alternatives with different strength/corrosion trade-offs.
Actual chloride chemistry, temperature, flow, crevice conditions, design code and exact product form.

Recommendation_Rules: If grade_application evidence directly supports the application, pass. If only weak/context evidence exists, mark Needs verification rather than automatic pass/fail.
Reject only when supplied evidence clearly contradicts the required environment. Missing corrosion data => Needs verification.
If user temperature exceeds documented grade/application capability, reject. If capability is not documented, flag Needs verification.
Compare minimum YS/UTS target with source-supported minimums where comparable product form/standard applies.
If welding is required, prefer grades with explicit weldability evidence; missing data => Needs verification.
Use product_forms field; if required form is not listed, flag verification rather than invent availability.
Use prototype relative cost band only after engineering eligibility. Cost must not override a failed hard requirement.
Increase weight for the user-selected critical property such as corrosion or strength; keep hard constraints unchanged.
Do not score unsupported properties as zero; renormalize available weights or flag the result conditional.
Every important recommendation reason should retain grade/source/page references.
